what: The pressure probability P(spread > tau) at h = 1, Brier, the published exceedance predictor with and without the curve-implied spread, against calendar climatology and the persistence-logistic model. The secondary result is tau = +5 bp; it is not part of the pass rule.

with_without.sign_convention: difference = brier(gbm) - brier(gbm_curve_implied_spread) on each scored day; a positive mean means gbm_curve_implied_spread had the lower Brier score, so it beat the benchmark on these days

model_a.sign_convention: difference = brier(calendar_climatology) - brier(gbm) on each scored day; a positive mean means gbm had the lower Brier score, so it beat the benchmark on these days

model_b.sign_convention: difference = brier(calendar_climatology) - brier(gbm_curve_implied_spread) on each scored day; a positive mean means gbm_curve_implied_spread had the lower Brier score, so it beat the benchmark on these days

model_a.sign_convention: difference = brier(persistence_logistic) - brier(gbm) on each scored day; a positive mean means gbm had the lower Brier score, so it beat the benchmark on these days

model_b.sign_convention: difference = brier(persistence_logistic) - brier(gbm_curve_implied_spread) on each scored day; a positive mean means gbm_curve_implied_spread had the lower Brier score, so it beat the benchmark on these days
